surfaces.copy: A public RIASEC summary shows the Holland code and six 0–100 interest dimension scores from this assessment. Share the link only if you are comfortable making this information public. It does not establish ability, job fit, or a career conclusion.
The share page is not a full report and is not career advice. It keeps only a minimal interest-clue summary and method boundary, and must not be used to judge ability, job fit, or stable identity.

A personal PDF is only a saved copy of this result: it keeps the assessment snapshot, generation time, and necessary method boundary once, without adding new career judgments. Once forwarded, the platform cannot remotely recall it.

A counselor discussion PDF is for shared reading with user permission: it keeps a small exploration summary and the necessary limits, then turns them into next observation questions. It must not be used for screening, admission, promotion, elimination, or qualification decisions.

History lists completed attempts with the form information and Holland code provided for each saved result, plus links to the formal result, sharing, and retaking when available. Open the reports to read their six dimensions, close scores, and response-quality notes. The list does not calculate change, establish a stable identity, or show ability gains or losses.
60Q and 140Q use different score spaces. History may note which clues each snapshot emphasized, but it must not compare raw-score gains or drops or say the interest profile improved or declined.

A cautious-reading public summary may still show the Holland code and six 0–100 interest scores. Share it only if you are comfortable making these visible, and treat the result as tentative interest clues rather than a career or ability conclusion.

v5_editorial_note: English share/PDF/history lifecycle draft keeps RIASEC as an interest-signal assessment and requires human review before broad content expansion.
